q: A table is partitioned by month on `created_at`. Which query opens only ONE partition?
options: `WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' AND created_at < '2026-06-01'`
`WHERE user_id = 5`
`WHERE date_trunc('month', created_at) = '2026-05-01'`
`WHERE payload LIKE 'a%'`
why: The WHERE must compare the plain partition column. A function around it, or another column, leaves Postgres no way to skip drawers (I tested all three).

q: Why does a `PRIMARY KEY (id)` fail on a table partitioned by `created_at`?
options: id cannot be a bigint on a partitioned table
Each partition has its own index, so a unique rule must include the partition column
Partitioned tables cannot have primary keys at all
The key must be a text column
why: The fix is `PRIMARY KEY (id, created_at)`. The cost: id alone is no longer unique for the whole table.

q: You must remove 100,000 old rows from a huge partitioned table. What is the best way?
options: Run a big DELETE, then VACUUM FULL right away
Run a big DELETE and let autovacuum shrink the file
Drop the old partition (DETACH, then DROP)
Run UPDATE to set the rows to NULL
why: Dropping a partition deletes its file at once, in milliseconds, with no dead rows. A DELETE leaves dead rows and a file that stays the same size.

q: An insert fails with `no partition of relation ... found for row`. What is a fix?
options: Set `max_connections` higher
Add an index on the partition column
Run ANALYZE on the table
Create the missing partition (ahead of time with a job), or add a DEFAULT partition as a safety net
why: No drawer fits the row's date. Watch a default partition: if it fills up, your monthly job stopped.

q: What is the main difference between partitioning and sharding?
options: Partitioning splits a table on ONE server. Sharding puts the parts on DIFFERENT servers
Partitioning is for writes, sharding is for reads
Sharding keeps JOINs working, partitioning does not
There is no difference, the words mean the same
why: On one server, JOINs, transactions and unique rules still work. Across servers, they break.

q: You shard by `hash(user_id) % 4` and add a 5th shard. About how many rows must move?
options: About 20%
About 80% of them
None, only the new shard's rows
About 1%
why: The remainder changes for almost every id (80,017 of 100,000 in my test). Hash into many buckets with an owner table instead: only about 20% moved.

q: A table has one slow query and 800 GB of data. What do you try BEFORE sharding?
options: Shard it into 8 servers at once
Move everything to JSONB columns
Read the plan and add an index, then a cache or a replica, then partition, then a bigger machine
Turn off autovacuum
why: Sharding is the last step. It takes away cross-shard JOINs, transactions and unique rules, and moving data is slow.
